subject: RetailBot: urgent inference latency spike — path triage & exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: 20–40s inference latencies and 5xx from your hosts — RetailBot impact

Jonas / Marissa,

We started seeing a large spike in latencies and 5xx errors hitting Redwood endpoints from our production fleet at ~08:45 PST. Impact: roughly 12% revenue decline across our checkout funnel and a surge of support tickets. This is affecting multiple regions (us-west primarily).

Short summary:
- 08:45-09:05 PST: median inference latency jumped from ~180ms to 12–20s, peak 40s.
- Errors: 502/504 spike across our calls to model routes (we can forward logs).
- We've seen retries & backoffs cause queueing on our side.

We need an immediate triage and executive sync. Can your team confirm whether this is a model-serving issue, or network (VPC peering/DNS/firewall/proxy) on Redwood’s side? We have traces and a sampling of requests attached.

Attaching: retailbot-trace-0501.json (request spans + customer-side timing).

Please escalate — Sandeep and I will join any call.

— Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform
RetailBot

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: 20–40s inference latencies and 5xx from your hosts — RetailBot impact

Thanks Alex — we see the thread and are on it. I’m standing up a dedicated triage, looping infra and account. Early notes: your traces look like request TCP handshakes are completing but there’s tail latency during the TLS handoff and several hops show long DNS lookup times.

Immediate steps we’re executing:
- Enabling extended debug on the customer-facing load balancers (resource: redwood-sla-dashboard-0501.png attached).
- Capturing DNS resolver RTTs and authoritative lookups for your customer routes.
- Verifying VPC peering health & NAT session counters for the affected subnets.
- If network-side misroute is confirmed, we’ll fail traffic to an alternate peering path and roll back when stable.

I’ll coordinate the exec sync at 16:00 UTC (4:00 PM UTC) unless you need earlier. Vanessa — can you confirm whether RetailBot expects procurement / billing outreach if we need to apply a credit?

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: 20–40s inference latencies and 5xx from your hosts — RetailBot impact

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 09:22 AM Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com> wrote:
> Early notes: your traces look like request TCP handshakes are completing but there’s tail latency during the TLS handoff and several hops show long DNS lookup times.

Quick triage update from infra:
- DNS: Our internal resolver pool (resolver-us-west-2-b) shows intermittent TTL spikes and repeated retries to upstream resolvers between 08:43–09:10 PST. We captured ~76 timed-out queries that correlate with RetailBot prefixes. (see attachment: dns-resolver-logs-0501.tar.gz)
- NAT / conntrack: For one peering host cluster we observed conntrack table exhaustion and heavy SNAT churn which can lead to retransmit storms; counters climbed ~94% above baseline.
- Proxy: A small subset of proxied requests entered the slow path due to an unexpected header size growth from retries, triggering extra validation.

Immediate mitigation options we propose (order of operational risk):
1) Flip RetailBot routes to alternate peering (low risk, 3–5 minute window to validate).
2) Temporary increase conntrack limits and drain affected NAT instances (medium risk, requires short rolling restart).
3) Apply targeted DNS resolver bypass for RetailBot domains to authoritative lookups (higher risk if misconfigured).

We need sign-off to do (1) now. If we get approval, infra can make the route update and monitor for 15 minutes.

Rishi
Staff Engineer, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 10:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: 20–40s inference latencies and 5xx from your hosts — RetailBot impact

Alex — thanks for flagging. I’ve booked a 45-minute exec sync for 16:00 UTC (link: https://meet.google.com/redwood-retailbot-0501) to walk through the timeline and remediation plan.

Also: we are prepared to offer a one-off credit for the impact window. I’ve attached the proposed credit memo (proposed-credit-0501.pdf). Procurement contact included? If so, please loop them into this thread or share procure@retailbot.com and I’ll start the approval.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: RetailBot — urgent path triage and ask for exec approval (summary)

Vivek — fyi and request for quick decision. RetailBot (DBL-7843) is experiencing a severe production latency and error surge tied to network path instability between our edge proxies and the customer's VPC peer. Key points: 

- Impact window: 08:45–09:25 PST. Customer reports ~12% hour-over-hour revenue impact for that window.
- Triage findings (infra): DNS resolver retries + conntrack exhaustion on one peering cluster; small percentage of proxied requests entered slow-path validation.
- Proposed immediate action: flip traffic for RetailBot to alternate peering (Option 1 proposed by infra). We estimate 3–5 minutes to cutover with ~15 minutes of monitoring before declaring stable.
- Secondary action: increase conntrack limits and rotate NAT instances (requires orchestration lead and 10–20 minute rolling restarts).
- Business ask: sign-off for the cutover now and approval to apply a one-off customer credit (Vanessa has proposed memo).

I’m prepared to execute the cutover once we have your go-ahead. I’ll be on the exec sync at 16:00 UTC — joining with Rishi and infra leads.

Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@retailbot.com>, procure@retailbot.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RetailBot: urgent inference latency spike — path triage & exec sync

Thanks — 16:00 UTC works for us. We’ll join from the platform and CTO side.

For the cutover: please confirm expected behavior for in-flight requests and whether retries will be deduplicated on your side or if we should implement a short client window to avoid double-execution. We’ll also need a formal credit confirmation for our finance team for the impact window.

Appreciate the fast response — this is material for our ops team, and we’ll escalate internally if we don’t see stabilization post-cutover.

— Alex

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:52:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RetailBot: urgent inference latency spike — path triage & exec sync

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 15:47 UTC Alex Morgan <alex@retailbot.com> wrote:
> For the cutover: please confirm expected behavior for in-flight requests and whether retries will be deduplicated on your side or if we should implement a short client window to avoid double-execution.

Quick operational note: our serving tier will accept idempotency keys and attempt best-effort deduplication for in-flight retries, but we cannot guarantee perfect dedupe for every edge case. Recommend you enable a 30s client-side retry window and rely on our idempotency for anything beyond that. We will prioritize draining the old peering path to reduce overlap.

Thanks everyone — on standby to proceed once leadership signs off.

Jonas
